# Fix: PR #7337 — CI red, `test_repo_test_suite_is_clean` lint failure

CI's `Pytest fastlane` job failed on `tests/test_lint_test_assertions.py::test_repo_test_suite_is_clean`:

```
AssertionError: Found stale pinned epic assertions in tests: [
  AssertionViolation(path='tests/api/test_app_factory.py', line_number=265,
    snippet='assert third_client.get("/api/session-streams/v1/status/epic:4707").status_code == 404',
    epic_id='epic:4707', reason="hard-coded stream literal 'epic:4707' in assertion; derive from
    issue_streams.yaml or use a designated fixture pattern (e.g. # noqa: epic-id,
    # allow-hardcoded-epic: <reason>, or synthetic epic ID)"),
  AssertionViolation(path='tests/api/test_app_factory.py', line_number=266, ... same for /digest/epic:4707)
]
```

Your new regression test (the one reproducing grok's live probe) added assertions on
`tests/api/test_app_factory.py:265-266` using the literal `epic:4707` — matching the project's
own house lint that forbids a hardcoded epic-ID literal in a test assertion unless annotated.
Other tests in this same PR (`tests/test_session_streams_api.py`, per the design pattern already
established elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. `session_router.py`'s own tests) use the
`# allow-hardcoded-epic: <reason>` trailing-comment convention for exactly this case — a synthetic
test-fixture epic ID with no real registry meaning, used only to exercise a code path.

## Fix

Add `# allow-hardcoded-epic: <short reason>` to the end of both flagged lines
(`tests/api/test_app_factory.py:265` and `:266`) — a reason like "synthetic epic id for the
missing-DB 404 regression probe, not a real registry epic" (or your own equally accurate short
reason) is fine. Do not change the epic number or the assertion logic — this is purely the
required annotation.

**Before pushing:** run `tests/test_lint_test_assertions.py::test_repo_test_suite_is_clean`
yourself and confirm it passes (this is the exact test that failed in CI — reproduce it locally,
don't just add the comment and hope). Also re-run `tests/api/test_app_factory.py` and
`tests/test_session_streams_api.py` to confirm nothing else broke.

Push to the SAME branch (`agy/monitor-7269-step1-session-streams-cluster`). This is a mechanical,
single-file, two-line annotation fix — no re-review of the underlying logic is needed since
nothing behavioral changes; the driver will re-check CI directly rather than dispatching a full
re-review round for this one.
